q: A patient on clopidogrel needs femoral–popliteal bypass. What determines whether a spinal can be performed?
o: Timing of the last antiplatelet and anticoagulant doses against neuraxial guidelines
why: Plan antiplatelets and anticoagulants around neuraxial timing; otherwise use GA with peripheral blocks.

q: Why is heparin given before clamping during lower limb bypass?
o: To prevent thrombosis in the clamped vessels and graft
why: Heparin prevents thrombosis while vessels are clamped; agree the plan and any protamine with the surgeon.

q: What BP should be maintained after lower limb bypass?
o: As low as possible to protect the graft
Adequate BP to maintain graft flow
why: Hypotension risks graft thrombosis; maintain BP and continue antiplatelets.

q: After lower limb revascularisation, a patient develops severe calf pain on passive stretch. What is the likely diagnosis?
why: Reperfusion can cause compartment syndrome; pain on passive stretch is an early sign. Fasciotomy is needed.

q: Which electrolyte rises in rhabdomyolysis and is the immediate threat to life?
why: Muscle necrosis releases potassium, phosphate, CK, myoglobin and urate; hyperkalaemia can cause arrhythmias.

q: What CK level is consistent with rhabdomyolysis?
why: CK over 1,000 IU/L or urinary myoglobin positive; treat with IV fluids and treat the cause.

q: Which CKD stage corresponds to an eGFR of 15–30?
why: Stages: I over 90, II 60–90, III 30–60, IV 15–30, V under 15.

q: Which opioid should be avoided in a patient with end-stage renal failure?
why: Morphine-6-glucuronide accumulates in renal failure; avoid tramadol too (largely renally excreted). Fentanyl and alfentanil are safer.

q: A patient with CKD on haemodialysis is listed for bypass. What should be checked before surgery?
o: Date of last dialysis, dry weight, potassium and fistula arm
why: Check timing of last dialysis, dry weight, electrolytes (especially K+), residual urine output and protect the fistula arm.

q: After bypass, which complication indicates graft failure requiring urgent return to theatre?
o: Loss of distal pulses with a cold limb
why: Loss of pulses and a cold limb suggests graft thrombosis; urgent re-exploration is needed.
